note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set.

checkers.alarm: `max|R^T R - I| > C * eps_d` or `|det R - 1| > C * eps_d` (entries are bounded by 1 and each is a sum of at most three products of unit-bounded factors)
checkers.invariant: the matrix `R` returned by `rotation3d` satisfies `R^T R = I` and `det R = +1`
checkers.precondition: any finite real angles `(x, y, z)`
checkers.rationale: head and MRI frames are related by rigid motions; a non-orthogonal block shears every sensor and source position.

checkers.alarm: as TRN-001 with tolerance `C * eps_d / max(w, 1e-3)`, `w = sqrt(1 - |q|^2)` (the real part is recovered through a square root whose conditioning is `1/w`)
checkers.invariant: `quat_to_rot(q)` satisfies `R^T R = I`, `det R = +1`
checkers.precondition: vector part `q` of a unit quaternion, `|q| <= 1` (the real part is `sqrt(1 - |q|^2)`)
checkers.rationale: head-position (cHPI) rotations are stored as quaternions.

checkers.alarm: `max|R' - R| > (C * eps_d + 2 * |R^T R - I|) / w^3` (the 3-component quaternion rebuilds `w` from `1 - |q|^2`)
checkers.invariant: `quat_to_rot(rot_to_quat(R)) = R`
checkers.precondition: `R` a proper rotation (`|R^T R - I| < 1e-8`, `det R > 0`) whose quaternion real part satisfies `w >= 1e-2` (`w^2 = (1 + tr R) / 4`)
checkers.rationale: both representations describe the same rigid orientation; coil orientation and head-movement tracking convert between them.

checkers.alarm: any of the six "zero" coordinates exceeds `C * eps_d * s`, or `x_lpa >= x_rpa`, or `y_nasion <= 0`, or the rotation block departs from orthonormal with `det = +1` by more than `C * eps_d * s / d`
checkers.invariant: the 4x4 transform from `get_ras_to_neuromag_trans` is a rigid motion that maps LPA and RPA onto the x-axis (`y = z = 0`, `x_lpa < x_rpa`) and the nasion onto the +y axis (`x = z = 0`, `y > 0`); the origin is the foot of the nasion perpendicular on the LPA-RPA line
checkers.precondition: finite non-collinear fiducials `nasion, lpa, rpa` with `rpa != lpa`; distance of the nasion to the LPA-RPA line `d >= 1e-6 * s`, `s = max|coordinate|` over the three points
checkers.rationale: every MEG/EEG source estimate is expressed in this frame (Neuromag convention); a wrong frame moves all sensors relative to the brain.

checkers.alarm: `|R a - b|`, `max|R^T R - I|` or `|det R - 1|` exceeds `C * (eps_d + delta) / sin(theta)` (the formula assumes unit vectors, so slack `delta` shifts the result by about `2 delta`; the rotation axis `a x b` carries absolute error `eps_d` and its direction error is amplified by `1/sin(theta)`)
checkers.invariant: `R = _find_vector_rotation(a, b)` is a proper rotation and `R a = b`
checkers.precondition: `a`, `b` unit vectors (norm within `1e-12` of 1, total slack `delta`) with `sin(theta) >= 1e-8`, `theta` the angle between them
checkers.rationale: it orients electrode and arrow glyphs, and the same construction orients dipoles. Known limitation (N): exactly (anti)parallel inputs take a separate branch and are excluded by the `sin(theta)` fence.

checkers.alarm: `|p - p'| > 8 * sqrt(eps_d) * |p|` per point (the polar angle comes from `arccos(z/r)` whose conditioning is `1/sin(theta)`, so near a pole the angle error reaches `sqrt(2 eps_d)`)
checkers.invariant: `_sph_to_cart(_cart_to_sph(p)) = p`
checkers.precondition: finite 3-D points with `1e-100 <= |p| <= 1e100`, float64
checkers.rationale: spherical-harmonic and spline warps work in these coordinates.

checkers.alarm: the rotation from the re-called average on `R_Q`-rotated inputs differs from `R_Q @ R_avg` by more than `C * eps_d * n / (gap * w_min^3)` (`n` quaternions summed into `A`; `w_min` the smallest real part before and after the rotation)
checkers.invariant: for a fixed rotation `R_Q`, `avg(R_Q R_i) = R_Q avg(R_i)`
checkers.precondition: `quats` (n, 3) with weights `>= 0`, positive sum; every quaternion has `w >= 1e-2` before and after left-multiplying by the fixed rotation `R_Q`; the gap of the two largest eigenvalues of the accumulator `A = sum w_i^2 q_i q_i^T` (the implementation scales `q` by the normalised weight before forming the outer product) is `gap >= 1e-6 * trace(A)`
checkers.rationale: the mean head position over a recording must not depend on which coordinate frame the individual positions are expressed in.

checkers.alarm: `max|diff| > C * eps_d / w_min`, `w_min` the smallest of the three real parts
checkers.invariant: `quat_to_rot(_quat_mult(a, b)) = quat_to_rot(a) @ quat_to_rot(b)`
checkers.precondition: unit-quaternion vector parts `a`, `b` with real parts `>= 1e-4`, and a product real part of magnitude `>= 1e-4`
checkers.rationale: composing head movements must equal composing the rotations they represent.

checkers.alarm: some `reject_i` with `p_adj_i > alpha (1 + C eps_d)`, or some `not reject_i` with `p_adj_i < alpha (1 - C eps_d)`
checkers.invariant: `reject_i` holds iff `p_adj_i < alpha`
checkers.precondition: p-values in `[0, 1]`, `alpha` in `(0, 1)`, either method
checkers.rationale: the two outputs describe the same Benjamini-Hochberg/Yekutieli decision; disagreement changes which tests are reported significant.

checkers.alarm: any violation beyond `C * eps_d * max(p_adj, p)`
checkers.invariant: `p_adj_i >= p_i`, `p_adj_i <= 1`, and `p_i <= p_j` implies `p_adj_i <= p_adj_j`
checkers.precondition: p-values in `[0, 1]`
checkers.rationale: step-up adjusted p-values are monotone in the raw p-values and never smaller.

checkers.alarm: a Bonferroni rejection not rejected by BH, or `p_adj_bonf < p_adj_bh - C eps_d`
checkers.invariant: a family-wise-error control rejects a subset of what the FDR control rejects, and its adjusted p-values are not smaller
checkers.observation_point: return of `bonferroni_correction`; the checker re-calls `fdr_correction(pval, alpha, "indep")`
checkers.precondition: p-values in `[0, 1]`
checkers.rationale: FWER control implies FDR control; the reverse ordering means one of the two procedures is mis-implemented.

checkers.alarm: as STAT-003 with the two methods
checkers.invariant: rejections under `"negcorr"` are a subset of those under `"indep"`, and adjusted p-values are not smaller
checkers.observation_point: return of `fdr_correction`; the checker re-calls it with the other method
checkers.precondition: p-values in `[0, 1]`
checkers.rationale: the harmonic correction factor is `>= 1`.

checkers.alarm: any `p < 1/B - eps_d`
checkers.invariant: a permutation p-value is never below `1/B` (the observed labelling is one of the `B` permutations)
checkers.observation_point: return of `_pval_from_histogram` as used for cluster p-values
checkers.precondition: a finite surrogate distribution `H0` of `B = len(H0)` statistics produced by the permutation test (index 0 is the observed labelling)
checkers.rationale: a permutation p-value of 0 would claim certainty from a finite resampling.

checkers.alarm: `max|h - h[::-1]| > C * eps_d * N * max|h|`
checkers.invariant: the impulse response is symmetric, `h[k] = h[N-1-k]` (constant group delay `(N-1)/2`)
checkers.precondition: `_construct_fir_filter` with `phase` in `{linear, zero, zero-double}`
checkers.rationale: zero-phase filtering of evoked responses relies on a symmetric kernel to avoid latency shifts.

checkers.alarm: `||a - b||_2 > C * eps_d * log2(n_fft) * ||x||_2 * ||h||_2 + max|FFT(h - h[::-1])| * ||x||_2` per channel (the second term is the asymmetry the precondition admits)
checkers.observation_point: return of `_overlap_add_filter`; the checker re-calls it on the reversed data with every argument forwarded
checkers.precondition: `_overlap_add_filter` with `phase="zero"`, a symmetric `h` (FLT-001 tolerance), finite data
checkers.rationale: a zero-phase filter must treat past and future identically; asymmetry means a latency shift.

checkers.invariant: `filt(x + y) = filt(x) + filt(y)` (linear time-invariant system)
checkers.observation_point: return of `_overlap_add_filter`; re-called on `x + y` and `y`
checkers.precondition: `_overlap_add_filter`, finite data `x`, with `y = x[..., ::-1]`
checkers.rationale: band-limiting must commute with averaging and subtraction of conditions.

checkers.invariant: `resample(x + y) = resample(x) + resample(y)`, `y = x[..., ::-1]`
checkers.observation_point: return of `resample`; re-called with every argument forwarded
checkers.precondition: `resample` with finite data, either method
checkers.rationale: a data-dependent normalization would make condition differences change under resampling.

checkers.alarm: `|sum W| > 1e-4 * sum|W|`
checkers.invariant: `sum_k W_k = 0` (admissibility criterion for the continuous wavelet transform; the 5-sigma truncation and sampling leave at most `1e-4` of the absolute mass)
checkers.precondition: `morlet(..., zero_mean=True)` with `sigma_t * sfreq >= 2` (sampling resolves the envelope) and `f < sfreq / 2` (the oscillation is not aliased)
checkers.rationale: a wavelet with non-zero mean leaks the DC offset into every frequency.

checkers.alarm: `|PSD(2x) - 4 PSD(x)| > C * eps_d * 4 * PSD(x)` per bin (scaling by a power of two is exact in IEEE arithmetic, so only data-dependent normalization can break it)
checkers.invariant: `PSD(2 x) = 4 PSD(x)` (V^2/Hz)
checkers.observation_point: return of `psd_array_multitaper`; re-called on `2 x` with every argument forwarded
checkers.precondition: `psd_array_multitaper`, finite data with `1e-100 <= |x| <= 1e100`
checkers.rationale: spectral power must scale as amplitude squared.

checkers.alarm: the measured concentration `d^T B d / d^T d` (`B_nm = sin(2 pi W (n-m)) / (pi (n-m))`, `B_nn = 2W`) differs from the returned eigenvalue by more than `1e-6`, or is `<= 0.9 - 1e-6` when `low_bias`
checkers.invariant: each returned taper carries the fraction `lambda_k` (the returned eigenvalue) of its energy in the band `|f| <= half_nbw / N`, and with `low_bias=True` every retained `lambda_k > 0.9` (not when no taper reaches 0.9: the library then warns and keeps the best one)
checkers.precondition: `dpss_windows` with `sym=True`, `2 <= N <= 2048`
checkers.rationale: multitaper bias bounds rest on the tapers' leakage property.

checkers.alarm: a negative variance beyond `C eps_d |C|_max`, an asymmetry above `C eps_d |C|_max`, or the scaled minimum eigenvalue below the bound; all three bounds are multiplied by `max(1, max_i m2_i / C_ii)` where `m2_i` is the uncentred second moment the one-pass estimator subtracts the mean from
checkers.invariant: `C = C^T` and every eigenvalue of `D^{-1/2} C D^{-1/2}` (`D = diag(C)`, restricted to channels with positive variance) is `>= -C * n * eps_d`; no variance is negative
checkers.precondition: `compute_covariance` / `compute_raw_covariance` results with a full (2-D) matrix, `n <= 2000`
checkers.rationale: a covariance with negative variance has no valid whitener and breaks every downstream inverse and beamformer.

checkers.alarm: `|variance - 1| > C * eps_d * n_chan * kappa`
checkers.invariant: under the noise model `x ~ N(0, S)`, the noise-normalized estimate has unit variance per source: `noisenorm_i^2 * sum_c (K_c S K_c^T) = 1` (sum over the orientation components `c` of source `i`)
checkers.precondition: `_apply_inverse` with `method="dSPM"`, `pick_ori` in `{None, vector}` (free or fixed orientation); the noise covariance is a 2-D matrix and the prepared whitener whitens it (`max|Wp S Wp^T - I_r| <= 1e-6`, `Wp = whitener @ proj`); `kappa` of its retained spectrum `<= 1e6`
checkers.rationale: dSPM statistics are interpreted as z-like scores; a wrong normalization misstates significance.

checkers.alarm: `|s - |v|| > C * eps_d * n_chan * max|s|` per source and time
checkers.invariant: the combined estimate equals the Euclidean norm of the three components returned with `pick_ori="vector"`
checkers.precondition: `_apply_inverse` with a free-orientation operator, `pick_ori=None`, method in `{MNE, dSPM, sLORETA}`
checkers.rationale: the two output modes describe the same current vector.

checkers.alarm: `|S(2x) - 2 S(x)| > C * eps_d * 2 |S(x)|` elementwise
checkers.invariant: applying it to `2 x` gives `2 *` the estimate for `x` (scaling by two is exact, so only a data-dependent step can break it)
checkers.observation_point: return of `_apply_inverse`; re-called on the scaled evoked
checkers.precondition: `_apply_inverse`, method in `{MNE, dSPM, sLORETA}`, finite data
checkers.rationale: linearity underlies averaging before localization and the interpretation of amplitudes.

checkers.alarm: `max|W_k g_k - I| > C * eps_d * kappa(G_k^T C^+ G_k) * max(1, |g_k|^2 |C^+| / |G_k^T C^+ G_k|)`
checkers.invariant: the spatial filter passes a unit source at its own location undistorted, `W_k g_k = I` (`g_k` the effective lead field after orientation selection)
checkers.precondition: `_compute_beamformer` with `weight_norm=None`, `reduce_rank=False`, `orient_std = 1`, `inversion="matrix"` or a single orientation, and the per-source denominator `G_k^T C^+ G_k` with condition number `<= 1e6` (the library inverts it with an eigenvalue cutoff of `1e-7` of the largest, which is a deliberate pseudo-inverse above that)
checkers.rationale: the constraint defines the LCMV beamformer; failing it biases source amplitude.

checkers.alarm: data differ by more than `C * eps_d * n * M` (`M` the largest absolute value among the inputs and the result: opposite-sign inputs cancel) or `nave` differs by more than `C * eps_d * nave`
checkers.invariant: pooling two groups and then the pooled result with the third equals pooling all three: same data and same `nave`
checkers.observation_point: return of `combine_evoked`; the checker re-calls it in nested form
checkers.precondition: `combine_evoked` with `weights="nave"` and three or more inputs sharing channels and times
checkers.rationale: the effective number of averages sets the noise level used in inverse regularization.

checkers.alarm: for any source, `||G r_hat|| > 1e-8 * max(||G t1||, ||G t2||)` with `t1, t2` an orthonormal tangent basis (cancellation amplification is bounded by `(r_sensor / r_dipole)^3 <= 8e6`, times `eps_d`)
checkers.invariant: the external magnetic field of a current dipole oriented along `rr - r0` is zero
checkers.observation_point: the gain matrix from the forward computation
checkers.precondition: a spherical conductor model (sphere centre `r0`), MEG channels, source positions at least 1 mm from `r0`, inside the sphere
checkers.rationale: the classic invariant that makes MEG blind to radial sources.

checkers.alarm: `max|P - P^T|` or `max|P^2 - P| > C * eps_d * n_channels`
checkers.invariant: the operator `P` is symmetric and idempotent, `P = P^T`, `P^2 = P`
checkers.precondition: `make_projector` with at least one included projector, `nproj < n_channels` (`nproj` is the returned rank: directions with singular value above `1e-2` of the largest)
checkers.rationale: applying an artifact projector twice must not change the data a second time.

checkers.alarm: `max|U^T U - I|`, `max|P U|` or `|trace(I - P) - nproj|` above `C * eps_d * n_channels`
checkers.invariant: the returned basis `U` has orthonormal columns, `P U = 0`, and the removed dimension `trace(I - P)` equals `nproj`
checkers.precondition: as PRJ-001
checkers.rationale: the number of projectors reported and applied must match the dimension removed.

checkers.alarm: `|F - F_centred| > C * eps_d * n_total * (sum x^2 / SS_within) * max(|F|, 1)` per column, or a non-finite `F` while `F_centred` is finite (the sums of squares are formed from raw sums, whose cancellation grows like the ratio of total to within-group sum of squares)
checkers.invariant: adding a constant `c` to every observation leaves F unchanged
checkers.observation_point: return of `f_oneway`; the checker re-calls it on the data minus the per-column grand mean
checkers.precondition: `f_oneway` with `sigma = 0`, at least two groups of at least two samples (any numeric dtype, integers included), finite data, non-zero within-group variance, `C * eps_d * n_total * (sum x^2 / SS_within) <= 1` (cancellation not catastrophic), `eps_d` the eps of the float dtype of the data (float64 for integers)
checkers.rationale: group differences cannot depend on the recording baseline.

checkers.alarm: as STAT-006 with `|F - t^2|`
checkers.invariant: `F = t^2`, `t` from `ttest_ind_no_p(a, b)` (equal variances)
checkers.precondition: `f_oneway` with exactly two groups, `sigma = 0`, at least two samples each, non-zero within-group variance
checkers.rationale: two independent routes to the same test must agree.

checkers.alarm: `| |H(f_c)| - 0.5 | > 0.02` (three times the weakest listed window deviation, 10^(-44/20) = 0.0063)
checkers.invariant: the magnitude response at the cutoff is 0.5 (documented: the cutoff is the -6 dB point, in the middle of the transition band)
checkers.precondition: `create_filter` with `method="fir"`, `fir_design="firwin"`, `phase="zero"`, exactly one cutoff (low-pass or high-pass), a transition band that fits between 0 and Nyquist around the cutoff
checkers.rationale: a wrong cutoff shifts the band of interest.

checkers.alarm: the L2 norm of `Re - x` (or of the shortfall `|x| - envelope` where positive) exceeds `C * eps_d * log2(n_fft) * ||x||_2`
checkers.invariant: `Re(analytic) = x` and the envelope is at least `|x|` everywhere
checkers.precondition: `_my_hilbert`, finite real `x`, `n_fft >= n_times`
checkers.rationale: the Hilbert envelope is used as instantaneous amplitude.

checkers.alarm: `max|W4 - W| > C * eps_d * kappa_C * kappa_den * max|W|`
checkers.invariant: scaling the data covariance by 4 (exact) leaves the spatial filters unchanged (the loading is proportional to `trace(C)`)
checkers.observation_point: end of `_compute_beamformer`; re-called with every argument forwarded and `4 * Cm`
checkers.precondition: `_compute_beamformer` with `weight_norm` in `{None, unit-noise-gain, unit-noise-gain-invariant}`, per-source denominators and the regularized covariance with condition numbers `<= 1e6`
checkers.rationale: filter weights are dimensionless; units of the covariance must not matter.

checkers.alarm: `max|row sums - 1| > C * eps_d * cond(C)`
checkers.invariant: each row of the interpolation matrix sums to one (a constant potential is interpolated to the same constant)
checkers.precondition: `_make_interpolation_matrix` with `alpha` in `[0, 1e-2]` and a bordered system `C` with `cond(C) <= 1e10`
checkers.rationale: interpolated bad EEG channels must not depend on the reference level.

checkers.alarm: `max|prior_2 - prior| > C * eps_d * max(prior)`
checkers.invariant: multiplying the whole gain matrix by 2 leaves the depth prior unchanged (the prior encodes relative sensitivity)
checkers.observation_point: return of `compute_depth_prior`; re-called on a copy of the forward with doubled gain
checkers.precondition: `compute_depth_prior` with a finite `limit` (not `None`)
checkers.rationale: units of the forward solution must not alter the localization prior. ### Revision log - 2026-10-27 FLT-005: the -6 dB point is the middle of the transition band given by the final control points (`freq`, `gain`) of the FIR design, not the user-facing `l_freq`/`h_freq`; both the 4-point low-pass and the 3-point high-pass layouts are covered. BF-001 and BF-002 share one checker (same lead-field/denominator derivation). Mutants that first missed were invalid faults, not checker defects: FLT-005 (gain error 0.005 is below the law's 0.02 resolution), TF-003 (taper rescaling and smooth ramps leave concentration unchanged to 1e-9; the resolution is 1e-6). Homogeneity and invariance laws (TF-002, FLT-003/004, INV-003, STAT-006, BF-002, DEP-001) cannot be tested by a multiplicative output perturbation (the re-call path is mutated identically) and use absolute offsets or scale-dependent logic edits. One more clean round is needed for two consecutive. ### Fresh-agent audit, Sonnet 5.5 (2026-10-28) 12 tests, 3 IDs triggered (TRN-003, TRN-007, TF-001); `fresh_sonnet55/`. All three were checker defects, none a library bug: - TF-001 fired only for frequencies above Nyquist (40 Hz at 50 Hz, 80 Hz at 100 Hz: ratio 1e-2; below Nyquist <= 6e-7). Added `f < sfreq/2` to the precondition (hook now passes `f`). - TRN-003: the round trip error is `~0.2 eps / w^3`, not `eps / w` (measured 5e-8, 4.7e-9, 4.6e-11 at w = 1e-3, 2e-3, 1e-2), because `quat_to_rot` rebuilds `w` from `1 - |q|^2`. Tolerance now `C eps / w^3`, precondition `w >= 1e-2`. - TRN-007: the checker's own re-call rotates the input through `rot_to_quat`, producing `w = 0.0108` and the same `eps / w^3` loss (diff 3.6e-12 vs tol 2e-13). Tolerance gets `1 / w_min^3`, precondition `w_min >= 1e-2`. - Why the earlier fuzz missed them: random rotations rarely have `w < 0.05`, and no input had a frequency above Nyquist. Fuzz generators now cover both. - Scorer: `scibench_pytest_plugin.py` flagged the library's lazy global `mne.utils.numerics._arange_div_impl` (None -> function on first call) as tampering in 6 tests (no effect on the score, but a false flag); None -> callable is no longer counted as a replacement. ### Fresh-agent audit, Sonnet 5.5 run 2 (2026-10-28, after the run-1 repairs) 4 tests, 3 IDs triggered (TRN-001, STAT-006, STAT-007); `fresh_sonnet55_run2/`. - TRN-001 (checker defect): `rotation3d` with float32/float16 angles returns a float64 matrix with only input-precision accuracy (orthogonality 9e-8 / 1.4e-3). The tolerance now uses the precision numpy promotes the angles to (`np.cos` of int16 -> float32, uint8 -> float16); the hook passes the angles. A later dtype sweep (float16/32/64, int16/32/64, uint8 over rotations, F test, FDR, resample, filter, multitaper, Hilbert) found no other dtype-dependent alarm. - STAT-006/007 (real library defect, reproduced on the pristine tree): `f_oneway` on int16 (or uint8) data returns F = -0.013 where float64/int32/scipy give 5.10, because `np.sum(a**2)` wraps around in the input integer dtype. int32 does not overflow for these values and does not alarm.
